segments.text: in this video you'll learn about cloudformationdrift
and why you should avoid it in infrastructure as code-based
applications so in order to understand why drift is a problem we first need to
review some basic infrastructure as code-based concepts so i think everyone
understands iec or infrastructure as code by now with iac you create your
infrastructure using a programming or templating language now this has a whole
bunch of benefits including making it easier to duplicate environments and
making infrastructure changes go through the code review process all in all
infrastructure as code is a powerful new paradigm that most new teams and
application developers are moving towards now one of the unsaid rules of
working with iac-based applications is that you're only ever supposed to change
your infrastructure through the code or the templating language that you're
using no more changing settings in a console ui or a cli everything needs to
be done through the code in order for you to maintain consistency but
unfortunately whether it be for testing or some kind of emergency hotfix someone
always ends up messing with the settings outside of the code and this is where
drift comes in now it's important to note that drift is a concept that can
apply to any iac provider and this includes things like aws cloudformation
and others such as terraform but in this video i'm going to focus on drift in the
context of aws cloudformation so now that we have some context let's quickly
review what cloudformation drift is so cloudformationdrift is when
infrastructure defined within your code is modified outside of that code so for
example if you create a dynamodb table or a lambda function using cloud
formation and someone comes and modifies with the settings of that lambda
function outside of that cloudformation template file that's when drift will
occur so it sounds pretty innocent like what's the problem with that but it
turns out there's a whole bunch of different problems that come with
cloudformationdrift the first one being update errors so this happens quite a
bit when people mess with settings in the console or through the cli things
like changing a particular setting or changing a permission for a resource to
access another resource these are seemingly innocent things at the time
that can result in some problems later now this doesn't seem that bad at face
value but trying to debug these errors that are result of cloud formation drift
can be very very frustrating and very time consuming so it's obviously
something you want to avoid now the other problem is that you compromise
your ability to replicate a stack so i think we all know one of the main
benefits of using infrastructure as code is that you can develop one stack in a
certain regional area and then pick that up and deploy that very easily into
another stack because all of those resources are defined using your code
now if you run into a scenario where you have drift between what your stack
actually is in code and what it is in reality then that becomes a problem for
replicating so that's another big problem with cloud formation drift and
the last reason is just a whole bunch of frustration and wasted time like i said
earlier you get a lot of cryptic errors it's very unclear what's actually wrong
with your stack when you encounter these kinds of scenarios and often it just
makes more sense to tear down the entire stack and then bring it back up again in
a fresh new state believe me i've been there and done that
so that's a little bit about what cloudformation drift is now i want to
talk about how to actually go about fixing drift now it turns out that
there's two distinct ways to solve drift in the context of cloudformation and any
other iac provider so assume that you have a resource that you created in
cloud formation or through infrastructure as code and then you
modify that resource maybe you change a setting like the memory utilization from
50 to 75. so one of the ways that you can fix this is that you can change what
you have in your code to match what the person did via the console so you can
change in your code base that setting that memory setting from 50 to 75 so
that it matches what exists in reality this is one way to do it and the other
way is pretty much the other way around modifying the setting of the resource
itself to match what you already have in your cloud formation or cdk code so
those are the two key ways to do this but the problem is like how do we know
exactly what changed now some of you may be able to figure this out through many
many hours of debugging cloudformation error logs and this certainly is
possible but there is a much better way that makes this a whole lot easier and
the answer is to use cloud formation drift detection so drift detection is a
relatively new feature so let's quickly talk about what it is and why it's
important so in essence drift detection is a tool that scans your cloud
formation stack and it's related resources to detect differences between
those two things this will tell you what is different between your infrastructure
as code based template and the resource itself as it exists in reality so in
order to use drift detection it's very very simple in cloud formation you just
head over to the console into your stack you go to the stack action settings like
you can see here and you just click on detect drift this will launch a wizard
where you just launch this process and eventually it'll spit out some results
whether or not drift was detected or not if drift was detected between what
cloudformation thought the resource should look like and what it actually
looked like so here's an example in this case here if we take a look at
some of the differences that cloudformationdrift identified we could
see there's three key ones here there's billing mode not equal the expected
value in our code was provisioned and the actual value was pay per request and
some of these settings are a little bit different as well as you can see here
and then within our template itself you can see it's highlighting the difference
you can see there's provisioned and paper request as we saw up here so this
was a little bit about what cloudformation drift is and why you
should avoid it if you want to learn more about cloud formation check out
these other videos on the left and right and thanks so much for watching i'll see
you next time
